questions.question: In the standard Shakura-Sunyaev model for a steady-state, geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk, how does the effective temperature $T_{\text{eff}}$ depend on the radial distance $r$ from the central compact object at radii far from the inner boundary ($r \gg r_{\text{in}}$)?
options: $T_{\text{eff}} \propto r^{-3/4}$
$T_{\text{eff}} \propto r^{-1/2}$
$T_{\text{eff}} \propto r^{-1}$
$T_{\text{eff}} \propto r^{-3/2}$

questions.question: Why is the primordial abundance of deuterium ($D/H$) considered the most sensitive 'baryometer' for determining the cosmic baryon density parameter ($\Omega_b h^2$) during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis?
options: Deuterium is created solely via neutrino-capture processes, making its synthesis independent of stellar contamination.

Deuterium fusion into $^3\text{He}$ and $^4\text{He}$ proceeds more efficiently at higher nucleon densities, making residual primordial $D/H$ a steeply decreasing function of the baryon-to-photon ratio.
Deuterium is immune to stellar destruction, allowing its observed abundance in low-metallicity systems to grow proportionally with baryon density.
Deuterium reaches nuclear statistical equilibrium at recombination, directly locking its final ratio to the decoupling temperature.

questions.question: The late-time Integrated Sachs-Wolfe (ISW) effect produces temperature anisotropies on large angular scales in the Cosmic Microwave Background. Why does this effect serve as direct observational evidence for dark energy?
options: Accelerated expansion causes gravitational potential wells to deepen over time, imparting a net blueshift to CMB photons exiting the wells.
Dark energy alters the Thomson scattering cross-section during the epoch of reionization, imprinting large-scale temperature-polarization correlations.
Accelerated cosmic expansion causes large-scale gravitational potential wells to decay, giving photons crossing them a net energy gain.
Dark energy increases the sound horizon scale at last scattering, shifting the first acoustic peak toward larger multipoles.

questions.question: According to Chandrasekhar's classical dynamical friction formula, how does the drag force $F_{\text{df}}$ exerted on a massive object of mass $M$ moving with velocity $v$ through a field of lighter stars scale with $M$ and $v$ (assuming $v$ is much larger than the velocity dispersion of the background stars)?
options: $F_{\text{df}} \propto M / v^2$
$F_{\text{df}} \propto M^2 v^2$
$F_{\text{df}} \propto M / v$
$F_{\text{df}} \propto M^2 / v^2$

questions.question: High-precision radial velocity observations of an exoplanetary system during a primary transit reveal the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect. Which physical property of the system is primarily derived from this measurement?
options: The sky-projected angle between the stellar rotation axis and the planetary orbital axis.
The atmospheric scale height and mean molecular weight of the transiting planet.
The true physical oblateness and spin rotation period of the transiting planet.
The absolute surface gravity and interior mass concentration of the host star.
